reading: Each green (3) outline box has a one-cell tab on one side. A mirror copy of the shape is drawn on the opposite side, reflected across the blank line just beyond the box (one-cell gap), coloured 1 if the reflection is left/right and 8 if up/down; copies are clipped at the grid edge.
verb: reflect each object away from its tab

slots.subject: each 3-coloured object (outline box with one-cell tab)
slots.axis: the empty row/column adjacent to the box side opposite the tab
slots.colour: 1 for a horizontal (left/right) reflection, 8 for a vertical (up/down) one

why: every added cell is the reflection of a shape cell across that line, in the axis-dependent colour

reading: The grid is split into four solid colour regions sprinkled with single noise cells of one colour. The output is a 1x1 grid of the colour of the region that contains the most noise cells.

slots.measure: number of noise (minority-colour) cells inside each region
slots.output: 1x1 grid of the colour of the region with the maximum count

why: the output colour is the region with strictly the most noise cells

reading: Each hollow rectangle's interior is filled with a checkerboard (starting at the interior's top-left cell) of the scattered colour whose number of scattered cells equals the checkerboard's cell count. All scattered single cells are erased.
verb: fill frame with checkerboard by count

slots.pattern: checkerboard with the interior's top-left cell coloured
slots.colour: the scattered marker colour whose cell count equals the number of coloured checkerboard cells
slots.markers: all isolated cells, cleared to background

why: per rectangle, count(markers of colour c) = number of checkerboard cells; markers removed

reading: Starting from the single 1 at the bottom-left, a diagonal line of 1 zigzags upward, bouncing between the left and right edges; every other cell becomes 8.

slots.start: the one 1 cell in the bottom-left corner
slots.path: one cell per row going up, column moving right then reflecting at each side wall

why: each row has exactly one 1, at the bounce-path column; rest 8

reading: The top-left 3x3 block (enclosed by the L of 5s) occurs exactly once elsewhere in the noisy grid; a 5x5 square outline of 5s is drawn around that occurrence.
verb: find copy of key and frame it

slots.target: the unique other exact occurrence of the key
slots.drawing: one-cell-wide 5 outline on the ring around the occurrence (5x5 box)

why: the ring around the unique exact match becomes 5; nothing else changes
invariants: all cells outside the drawn ring unchanged

reading: The grid is made of solid colour stripes (vertical or horizontal) with noise cells; every cell is reset to the majority colour of its stripe.

slots.stripes: maximal bands of rows or columns sharing one majority colour
slots.subject: every non-majority cell inside a stripe

why: every output row (horizontal stripes) or column (vertical stripes) is uniform and equals the input majority

reading: A vertical column of 5 splits the grid; the right half is folded over onto the left half (mirrored and overlaid), and the output is the left part without the separator.
why: output cell (r,c) = left(r,c) if non-zero else right(r, 8-c); output is the panel left of the 5 separator

reading: A 1 region sits above a jagged 6 region. In the column where the 1s reach deepest, the 1 cells become 9; in the column where the 6s rise highest (rightmost on a tie), the 1 cells become 4. Each line runs from the top of the 1 region down to the 6s.
verb: draw lines at deepest valley and highest peak

slots.line_9: the column where 1 extends lowest; all its 1 cells become 9
slots.line_4: the column where 6 extends highest (rightmost if tied); all its 1 cells become 4

why: only 1 cells in those two columns change, to 9 and 4 respectively

reading: The red (2) shape is a template; copies of it in red are stamped into some places where it fits entirely on background (0) cells among the 5s. Which fits get copies is unclear: overlapping fits are resolved to one, and one non-overlapping fit in pair 0 is not used.

slots.anchors: positions where the whole shape lands on 0 cells (a subset, non-overlapping)

why: every added cell is 2 and belongs to a translated copy of the template lying on former 0 cells

reading: Each green block is repeated diagonally downward in both directions: each new copy is shifted down by the block's height and left (or right) by its width, repeating until it leaves the grid.

slots.subject: each 3-coloured rectangle
slots.step: (+height, -width) and (+height, +width), applied repeatedly from each new copy
slots.extent: until the copies leave the grid (clipped)

why: every output 3 cell is in the original block or a copy at offset k*(h, +/-w) for k>=1
